title: Do This EVERY Time You Get Paid (Payday Routine)

dimension_notes.1_audience_topic_demand: EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE: no demand series stored. Payday and budgeting routines are evergreen personal-finance topics.
dimension_notes.2_differentiated_angle: Weak: a standard priority ladder (necessities, emergency fund, match, debt, Roth) framed as a payday routine.
dimension_notes.3_title: Clear imperative with a parenthetical keyword; promises a repeatable action.
dimension_notes.4_thumbnail: Stored 480x360 copy (letterboxed): bold PAYCHECK ROUTINE, a cartoon man (resembling a well-known cartoon father; rights not judged) and a coin-dispensing pipe feeding three containers, arrow. Very legible at mobile size.
dimension_notes.7_spine: Ordered priority ladder; closing automation step.
dimension_notes.9_emotion_credibility: Friendly and plain; credibility reduced by unsupported "90%" and credit-score thresholds.
dimension_notes.10_ending_cta: No closing CTA; the single ask is early.
dimension_notes.11_metadata_seo: Only title and spoken opening judged.
dimension_notes.12_editing_audiovisual: EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE: no video or audio forensics registered.

financial_checks.claim: $300/month from 25 at 8% = "around $1 million" at 65; from 35 = "about $400,000"; delay costs "around $600,000"
financial_checks.result: $1,047,000 and $447,000; difference $600,000. The $400,000 figure is rounded down by $47,000.

financial_checks.claim: 99% on-time payments is "good"; 97% makes you a "high-risk borrower"
financial_checks.result: Not verified; no published on-time-percentage cutoff exists that I know of; late payments are reported at 30+ days past due.

financial_checks.claim: Employer match is an "instant 100% return"; Roth gains are tax-free; capital-gains holding-period rule
financial_checks.result: Broadly correct; Roth rules omit eligibility and income limits.

strengths: Clear ordered ladder with correct arithmetic in the worked examples.
Plain analogies and an honest preference for the snowball method for behavioural reasons.
Automation step is the right per-payday action.
weaknesses: Title promises a per-payday action but most content is a one-off plan.
Subscribe ask before any value; no closing CTA.
Thumbnail three-way split is not the script's structure.
contradictions: "A routine ... every single time you get paid" versus a one-off priority ladder.
"About $400,000" at 35 versus the $447,000 its own inputs give.
improvement_opportunities: Re-title around the ladder ("The 7-Step Paycheck Order") or build the video around the payday automation step so the title is true.
State the credit-score point as "one 30-day late payment can drop a score" with a source, and drop the 90% claim.
Show the three-container split with the script's actual percentages on the thumbnail.
Move the subscribe ask after step 2 and add a closing next-video pointer.
